summary: Revision 2 of the S7c design against HEAD 2aafc0b5. All six review findings were verified against committed source and all six hold. (1) CRITICAL, confirmed: claim_due_recovery selects open obligations with deadline_at <= now() and next_attempt_at <= now() and spares a run only while an approval is requested/granted with consumed_at IS NULL; CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL sets consumed_at and never touches managed_run_terminalization_outbox; release_recovery_for_activity moves only next_attempt_at; the worker polls every second; only heartbeat_managed_agent_run renews deadline_at (MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS = 15 min, mirrored here) and the executor ignores its already_terminal reply. So a spent click makes a run recoverable within about a second whenever the human took more than 15 minutes (the normal case); the same window exists at HEAD in stage 1 but is milliseconds long, pre-consume widens it to the whole gateway-to-executor path. Fix: a spend-only consume (wire field omit_call) renews the run's obligation in the SAME transaction as the winning compare-and-set (same statement shape as the heartbeat, scoped by run_id and org_id, states open/processing only), so every spent click gets a full 15-minute window measured from the consume; it also skips the descriptor decrypt entirely. The renewal is tied to spend-only so the executor's own consume (switch-off path) is byte-identical. Recorded follow-up outside S7c: the executor must stop when the heartbeat reports already_terminal. (2) HIGH, confirmed: with the resume switch off the executor refuses before its own consume (continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, auth, connect), so the approval is still granted; the first design made typed non-terminalizing retryable:false frames apply to every continuation, which both changed committed behaviour (the committed InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied and connect-refused arms terminalize) and told clients a usable approval was spent. Fix: the new arms are gated on the attestation (resume.consumed_by_gateway), not on resume.is_some(); a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keeps the committed arms byte for byte; every new frame carries approval_spent:true and the contract states the two regimes. (3 and 5) HIGH, confirmed by grep: loop_resume_enabled, LOOP_RESUME_ENV and AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway do not exist at HEAD (AgentResume ends at segment_no = 8, reserved 9). The build is split: S7c-0 and S7c-A need nothing from S7b; S7c-B (continue_resume arity, the loop_resume_enabled() call, the attestation arm, contract tests, compose) has the hard precondition that S7b's proto field, loop_resume_enabled() and the executor honouring the attestation have landed. (4) HIGH, confirmed: prepare_resume in execution-core runtime_loop/agent.rs is the only Rust ConsumeApprovalRequest struct literal and has no ..Default::default(), so omit_call = 7 breaks execution-core; an explicit omit_call: false hunk lands in the same commit as the proto edit (owner: the lead's proto commit, S7b is also editing that function). (6) HIGH, confirmed: consume_then_launch borrows its consumer and cannot spawn, and the planned drop test passes without a spawn. Fix: spawn_consume_then_launch owns the consumer, holds the only tokio::spawn and returns a oneshot receiver; the test drops the receiver while the consumer is parked mid-RPC and the server side still commits; a source scan requires continue_run to call spawn_consume_then_launch( (never consume_then_launch( directly) and the helper to contain tokio::spawn(, with a durable_loop_contract guard and mutation. Kept from the first design: the order of checks, the closed vocabularies, the plan-grant decision (a continuation never reads or claims it), the BFF closed relay, the contract-before-UI rule, the consumed-approval predicate for RunDetail.resumable, and the live-proof ladder (now with a stale-deadline stage). No file was edited and nothing was run that mutates anything; fold.rs, agent.rs and loop_checkpoint.rs edits in flight were not read.
approach:
VERIFIED AGAINST COMMITTED SOURCE (HEAD 2aafc0b5; git show HEAD:path semantics, the in-flight fold.rs / agent.rs / loop_checkpoint.rs edits not read).

0. VERDICTS ON THE SIX FINDINGS
 F1 (recovery race) CONFIRMED and also true at HEAD for stage 1 (milliseconds there). Evidence by function: claim_due_recovery (candidate: state open AND deadline_at <= now() AND next_attempt_at <= now(), run not terminal, NOT EXISTS approval requested/granted with consumed_at IS NULL); has_pending_approval (same predicate, no expires_at test); release_recovery_for_activity (next_attempt_at only); run_recovery_worker (1 s sleep); CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL and store::consume_approval (never touch the outbox); heartbeat_managed_agent_run in the gateway-facing session-core (renews deadline_at = now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, state open, lease cleared, WHERE run_id AND state IN open/processing) versus the executor call site that discards the response. Fix in section I. The first design's 'recovery takes about 15 minutes' was false for a stale obligation and is rewritten: it is 15 minutes FROM THE CONSUME once section I lands.
 F2 (spent-state honesty) CONFIRMED. Committed behaviour for a continuation: InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied terminalize through terminalize_agent_dispatch_rejection_authenticated (frame agent_dispatch_rejected), a connect-phase Unavailable terminalizes as Unreachable (frame agent_dispatch_unreachable, retryable true), everything else is the degraded arm (agent_dispatch_unavailable). With the switch off those executor refusals happen BEFORE the executor's consume (enforce_resume, interceptors), so the approval is granted and unconsumed. Fix in section E: gate on the attestation.
 F3/F5 (build order) CONFIRMED by grep (no hit for consumed_by_gateway, loop_resume_enabled, LOOP_RESUME_ENV, EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED outside docs). Fix: three-part build order in steps.
 F4 (omit_call breaks execution-core) CONFIRMED: prepare_resume builds pb::ConsumeApprovalRequest with six explicit fields and no struct update; no Go literal exists outside gen/. Fix: explicit hunk.
 F6 (detach not protected) CONFIRMED by construction: consume_then_launch(&C, request, launch) cannot spawn, nothing is awaited between the consumer's answer and launch(), so the first design's drop test is vacuous. Fix in section B.

A. ORDER OF EVERY RPC AFTER S7c (resume switch on; with it off see the last paragraph)
 BFF: mint model, data-plane, inference, execution, session bearers (auth-core); org ZDR read; POST gateway /continue.
 Gateway: 1 continuation_gate (local). 2 continue_persistent_gate (local; ZDR and waived refused 409 not_resumable before anything is read). 3 body check (400 continue_incomplete). 4 bearer check (401 missing_bearer). 5 require_durable_run_owner_with_token (session-core). 6 GetRun (status, goal, thread_id, resumable). 7 GetApproval. 8 continue_preflight (local, refuses a consumed approval; no consume yet). 9 ONE detached task (spawn_consume_then_launch): ConsumeApproval with the user bearer (the same VerifiedModelBearer the executor later forwards as its session bearer; verified: spawn_run_dispatch is handed &model_bearer), step_id '', action_fingerprint '', claim_token as sent, omit_call true; session-core in ONE transaction: compare-and-set, renew the run's managed obligation (section I), commit; response consumed true. Only on consumed == true the task calls the launch closure (agentic_run_stream with the attested continue_resume). The handler awaits a oneshot. 10 inside the stream task: 'connected' frame; NO approved-plan claim; spawn_run_dispatch -> RunAgent; orchestration tail. 11 executor (S7b): enforce_resume, ConsumeApproval replay (same claim; reads the descriptor; consumed=false, already_consumed, same_claim; accepted because the attestation says the gateway sent exactly one RunAgent per won consume), then stage 1 or the in-place claim path, then heartbeat.
 Resume switch off (EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED unset at the gateway): steps 1-8 unchanged; step 9 is just launch() (agentic_run_stream with mode 'segment', consumed_by_gateway false, no pre-consume, no spawn); step 10 loses only the approved-plan claim (section D); step 11 as committed. The failure arms are the committed ones (section E). Exceptions to byte identity, stated honestly: (a) no plan claim and no plan block in goal when a plan is pending on the thread (a defect fix, shippable as the separate commit S7c-0), (b) the BFF relays closed codes instead of model_error for the gateway's 409/404. The RPC sequence to session-core's approval store and to execution-core is otherwise the committed one.

B. PRE-CONSUME RULES AND THE DETACHED TASK
 Answer map (pure fn preconsume_refusal(Result<bool, tonic::Status>) -> Result<(), PreconsumeRefusal>): Ok(true) proceed. Ok(false) (already consumed, whatever the claim, the SAME token included) -> 409 continuation_already_consumed (standing default: refuse every consumed approval). NotFound -> 404 approval_not_found. FailedPrecondition approval_not_granted | approval_expired | approval_not_resumable -> 409 same code; any other FailedPrecondition -> 409 not_resumable. InvalidArgument -> 400 continue_incomplete. PermissionDenied | Unauthenticated -> crate::http_routes::grpc_status_to_http (same as the owner check and reads). Unavailable | DeadlineExceeded | Internal | Unknown | Cancelled | Aborted | ResourceExhausted -> 503 continue_unavailable (ambiguous: the consume may have committed; on Internal from a failed renewal the transaction rolled back, still reported as ambiguous because the client cannot tell). Upstream messages are never echoed; logs carry the gRPC code and run_id only.
 Plaintext: the request sets omit_call = true; session-core then does not decrypt the descriptor at all (store spend-only intent, section I), returns consumed/already_consumed/same_claim only (consume_response also drops any call defensively). The gateway reads exactly one field, .consumed.
 Detach (finding 6): trait ApprovalConsumer { fn consume(&self, ConsumeApprovalRequest) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, tonic::Status>> + Send }. struct GrpcApprovalConsumer owns an OrchestrationCoreServiceClient<Channel> clone (state.orchestration_client.clone()) and an owned VerifiedModelBearer clone (verified Clone), no borrows. async fn consume_then_launch<C: ApprovalConsumer, T>(consumer: &C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal> stays the pure sequencing unit. fn spawn_consume_then_launch<C, T>(consumer: C, request: ConsumeApprovalRequest, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal>> where C: ApprovalConsumer + Send + 'static, T: Send + 'static is the ONLY place with tokio::spawn: it creates the oneshot, spawns an async move block that runs consume_then_launch(&consumer, request, launch).await and sends the outcome (ignoring a closed receiver), returns the receiver. agentic_run_stream returns Sse<ReceiverStream<..>> (Send, 'static) and spawns its own dispatch task, so once launch returns, RunAgent no longer depends on the handler. If the receiver is dropped the Sse is dropped with it; the stream task's sends are already ignored (let _ = tx.send), so the dispatch continues (whether follow_agentic_run exits early on a closed client channel is UNVERIFIED; dispatch itself does not depend on it). continue_run builds ONE launch closure (the single agentic_run_stream call in the body) and: resume off -> Ok(launch()); resume on -> match spawn_consume_then_launch(..).await { Ok(Ok(sse)) => Ok(sse), Ok(Err(Closed(s,c))) => continue_error, Ok(Err(Status(st))) => grpc_status_to_http, Err(_closed) => continue_error(503, continue_unavailable) }.
 Deploy order: executor image (S7b attestation honoured) first, then session-core (omit_call and renewal), then model-gateway, then flip EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED on both. New gateway with an old executor and the ledger off spends the click and fails with continuation_already_consumed. Gateway on with session-core old: omit_call is ignored by an old server, the response then carries the call (the gateway still reads only .consumed, but the decrypted call crosses to the gateway: deploy session-core first).

C. MODE CHOICE
 resume_mode_for(resume_enabled: bool, resumable: bool) -> &'static str: 'loop' only when both, else 'segment'; these two literals are the only place a mode is named. No other value is ever sent; segment_no stays 0; step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint, brief stay empty. The hint is advisory: the executor decides at claim time; a wrong hint costs a fallback to stage 1, never a refusal. Hint accuracy: session-core RUN_SELECT gains fold_pause_consumed = EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM approvals a WHERE a.run_id = r.id AND a.org_id = r.org_id AND a.idempotency_key = lc.pause_ref AND a.consumed_at IS NOT NULL); row_to_detail: resumable = old rule AND NOT (fold kind 'pause' AND fold_pause_consumed). pause_ref and approvals.idempotency_key are both format!(\"{run_id}:{step_id}\") (a DB test pins the pairing). park_reason is not read by S7c. Verified at HEAD: row_to_detail returns resumable to any viewer who can read the run and park_reason only to owner/service (RunDetail fields 17 and 18); run_detail_value in model-gateway http_routes is an allowlist without either (test-pinned here). DISCREPANCY kept open: at RPC level resumable is not owner-gated.

D. THE THREAD'S APPROVED PLAN: A CONTINUATION NEVER TOUCHES IT
 plan_context_wanted(plan_mode, resuming) = !plan_mode && !resuming gates approved_plan_context in agentic_run_stream. A /continue never calls take_approved_plan, never claims the plan, never injects it into goal, never reads granted_rung (dispatch_autonomy_rung(resuming) already states no rung). Reason: the approval pending on a thread belongs to a later execute turn; in-place ignores req.goal so a claim burns the single-use grant, stage 1 would inject it into a run that never held it. Consequence: the grant keeps its TTL for the next ordinary run. This applies to every continuation regardless of the switch (defect fix; shippable alone as S7c-0).

E. FAILURE CLASSIFICATION, GATED BY THE ATTESTATION (finding 2)
 let preconsumed = resume.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| r.consumed_by_gateway). The new arms apply only when preconsumed. Rationale: only then is the approval provably spent when the stream opens (the pre-consume won), so only then is 'no retry with a new token' true; and only then would a gateway terminalization be able to kill a run another segment owns. With preconsumed false, every arm is the committed one, byte for byte (terminalize on InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied and on connect refused; agent_dispatch_unavailable otherwise), and the approval stays usable exactly as today.
 For preconsumed: pure classify_continue_dispatch_failure(&tonic::Status) -> ContinueDispatchFailure { Refused(&'static str), Unreachable, Unknown }: Refused(token) when the code is NotFound (always approval_not_found), FailedPrecondition, Aborted, InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated and the message is in CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS; an unknown message there -> Refused(continue_refused) (never echoed); Unreachable = dispatch_never_reached_execution_core; Unknown = every other status, the follow deadline, a join error. Frames via continue_failure_event(request_id, run_id, &ContinueDispatchFailure) -> Event: ChatEvent::Error { code, message = code with spaces, retryable: false }, payload gains run_id and approval_spent: true. Refused(token) -> that token; Unreachable -> continue_unreachable; Unknown -> continue_outcome_unknown; local request-construction failure -> continue_refused. No terminalization in any of them. RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED is still published for Unreachable and Unknown, not for Refused. Placement: an arm Ok(Ok(Err(status))) if preconsumed BEFORE is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection; the three agent_dispatch_unavailable_event sites become dispatch_unknown_event(preconsumed, ..) (false returns the old frame); the Err(error) construction branch gets a preconsumed early path before its terminalization.
 What a pre-consumed continuation leaves behind and who ends it: the run is non-terminal, the approval is spent, and the managed obligation was renewed at the consume (section I), so session-core recovery terminalizes it 15 minutes after the consume if nothing heartbeats. Hence the failure matrix and live proof timings are 15 minutes FROM THE CONSUME.

F. CLIENT-VISIBLE VOCABULARIES (closed, test-pinned, owned by the gateway)
 HTTP, CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS (10): continue_disabled(409), not_resumable(409), continue_incomplete(400), missing_bearer(401), approval_not_found(404), approval_not_granted(409), approval_expired(409), approval_not_resumable(409), continuation_already_consumed(409), continue_unavailable(503). BFF relays 8 (all but continue_incomplete, which its own guard preempts, and missing_bearer, which maps to unauthorized). Owner-check and read failures keep grpc_status_to_http's flat body (BFF model_error). With the switch off, 409 continuation_already_consumed also arises from continue_preflight as at HEAD.
 Stream, CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS (19): executor-sourced continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, continuation_already_consumed, approval_not_found, approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable, approval_action_mismatch, approval_snapshot_mismatch, not_releasable, authority_widened, authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch, continue_space_scope_unsupported, continue_in_progress, resume_checkpoint_unavailable; gateway-made continue_refused, continue_unreachable, continue_outcome_unknown. These frames exist ONLY for a pre-consumed continuation and always carry approval_spent: true. Meaning: the approval is spent (by this request); no retry with a new claim token; follow the run through its events. continue_space_scope_unsupported and the authority_* tokens are unreachable through the gateway today (Space/pinned approvals are cold; the gateway states no wider authority) and stay as defence in depth. Frames agent_dispatch_unavailable / agent_dispatch_rejected / agent_dispatch_unreachable on a continuation (switch off) make NO claim about the approval and the contract says so (a retry with a new token is then permitted by the committed rules).

G. BFF
 proxy_sse_stream_with_data_plane (upstream.rs; verified: its status >= 400 branch today returns model_error, 401 -> unauthorized) gains a trailing relayed_errors: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)] (code, fixed message). The two upstream wrappers and chat/shared.rs (2 sites) and chat/streams.rs (1 site) pass &[]; orchestration.rs continue_run passes CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS. The branch: 401 -> unauthorized unchanged, else return upstream_error_response(resp, status, relayed_errors).await, a free function outside the relay body so tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs keeps scanning an unchanged byte path. Empty list: today's model_error without reading the body. Non-empty: read at most 4096 bytes, parse {error:{code}}, relay only a code in the list with the list's own message and the upstream status; flat string body, unlisted code, malformed or oversized stays model_error. Upstream messages are never relayed.

H. SPA CONTRACT (rule: contract before any UI wiring; none wired)
 The error vocabulary the client sees changes (model_error to closed codes), so chat.run.continue is updated first: new module src/shared/actions/chat-run-continue-contract.ts with the HTTP tuple (8 relayed), the frame tuple (19), chatRunContinueRefusalOf(input) (accepts ApiError-like {code,status} or an SSE error frame body {code, approval_spent}) and a per-code effect table. Two regimes written into it: a frame whose code is in the frame tuple and carries approval_spent true means spent, retryable false, followRun true; any other frame (including agent_dispatch_*) says nothing about the approval. HTTP effects: approvalSpent 'no' except continuation_already_consumed 'by_another' and continue_unavailable 'unknown'. The descriptor description states single use, closed refusals, no retry with a new token after a spent frame, and that the thread's plan grant is untouched. The input schema (runId, approvalId, claimToken) is pinned unchanged; continueRun keeps its signature; no UI caller is added.

I. RECOVERY DEADLINE RENEWAL AT THE CONSUME (finding 1)
 session-core store: new pub async fn consume_approval_spend_only(pool, id, org_id, run_id, user_id, action_fingerprint, claim_hash) and the existing consume_approval become two thin wrappers over a private consume_approval_with(.., intent: ConsumeIntent { Full, SpendOnly }) (the existing 7-argument consume_approval and its ~20 #[ignore] test call sites stay untouched). In SpendOnly: on the winning branch, before commit, run RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL: UPDATE managed_run_terminalization_outbox SET state = 'open', deadline_at = now() + ($3::bigint * interval '1 second'), next_attempt_at = now(), lease_owner = NULL, lease_token_hash = NULL, lease_expires_at = NULL, updated_at = now() WHERE run_id = $1 AND org_id = $2 AND state IN ('open', 'processing'), bound to MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS (terminalization.rs const made pub(crate), a one-word hunk). Zero rows affected is not an error (a run without an obligation). The descriptor is not read or decrypted in SpendOnly (call None) on either the winning or the replay branch. A database error rolls the whole transaction back, so the click is not spent. Only a WON spend-only consume renews (a replay or a lost race never extends a deadline). orchestration_grpc.rs consume_approval picks the intent from req.omit_call and builds the response through pure consume_response(done, omit_call). Lock order: the consume transaction locks the approval row then the outbox row and does not lock runs; recovery locks the run row then the obligation: no cycle. Effect: after a won pre-consume the obligation is open with deadline now + 15 min, the worker cannot claim it for 15 minutes, a 'processing' lease held earlier is cleared so recover_claimed_terminalization's state check fails safe. Abuse bound: one extension per consumed approval, owner-only. NOT in S7c (recorded follow-up, owner S7b or S3): the executor must stop when HeartbeatManagedRunResponse.already_terminal is true, before any dispatch (verified: the call site discards the response; already_terminal appears only in test doubles). Open: renew on the executor's own full consume as well (hardens HEAD stage 1 but changes the switch-off path).

J. CONSEQUENCES OF THE DECIDED DEFAULTS
 Refuse every consumed approval: a retry with the same token after a dropped connection is 409 continuation_already_consumed; recovery is the run's events, the unknown-outcome closers or the 15-minute recovery from the consume (S8 later). Waived runs: refused at continue_persistent_gate before anything is read. Widened request refused not narrowed: the gateway states nothing wider (no rung, floor 0, plan false, no Space, no route). Writer requires the ledger and a failed pre_effect save holds effects: nothing for the gateway; the live proof needs the ledger on.

invariants: The gateway consumes an approval at most once per /continue: only after every refusal check, only for a persistent turn, only with EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED on; only a won consume (consumed == true) proceeds; every other answer, the same claim token included, is 409 continuation_already_consumed.

Consume and launch are one detached task owned by spawn_consume_then_launch (the only tokio::spawn of the path): a client disconnect cannot spend an approval without RunAgent being sent. Test- and source-guarded.

A won spend-only consume renews the run's managed obligation deadline in the same transaction (open, deadline now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, lease cleared); a replay, a lost race or a full consume never renews. A spent click always has a full recovery window.

The gateway never holds a consumed call's content: omit_call is set, session-core does not decrypt or return it, one boolean is read, and logs carry the gRPC code and run_id only, never the claim token, an approval id's content or an upstream message.

The gateway never terminalizes an attested (pre-consumed) continuation; the new arms are gated on consumed_by_gateway, and a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keeps the committed arms byte for byte.

Every continuation frame carrying a code from CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS also carries approval_spent true and retryable false; a frame without it (agent_dispatch_* on a switch-off continuation) makes no claim about the approval.

The mode the gateway sends is 'loop' only with the switch on and RunDetail.resumable, else 'segment'; no other value; segment_no 0; hint fields empty; a wrong hint costs a stage-1 fallback and nothing else.
A continuation never reads, claims or injects the thread's approved plan or grant and states no rung, floor, Space, route or tools.
resumable and park_reason never reach a browser (run_detail_value is an allowlist); a pause fold whose approval is consumed is not resumable.

The BFF relays only a (status, code) pair from the closed list with its own fixed message; every other upstream error is model_error or unauthorized; SSE bytes are relayed untouched and the relay body still passes tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs.

The executor, not the gateway, owns what a continuation runs: tools, authority, mode and the approved call come from the paused snapshot; the executor's consume replay is the only reader of the descriptor.
